annotations.title: Sorted GEMM2 sustains up to five overlapping waves per SIMD
annotations.note: The traced target WGP reaches five wave slots per SIMD, compared with three for token-wave GEMM2. Active waves average 18.9k cycles versus 48.8k for token-wave. The sorted grid contains many quickly rejected blocks, but its active expert blocks carry less work per wave and expose more scheduling parallelism.

annotations.title: Sorting cuts GEMM2 L2 requests by 15.9%
annotations.note: The sorted path issues 1.478M TCC requests versus 1.758M for token-wave and records 1.388M misses versus 1.509M. Its lower hit rate is less important than avoiding duplicate routed-expert blocks.

annotations.title: Baseline GEMM2 pays heavy barrier and atomic stalls
annotations.note: The three active barriers at idx 111, 130, and 181 accumulate about 105.6k stall cycles, while atomics at idx 200/205/210/215 add about 17.4k. Main still wins because compacted expert blocks reduce total route work and its 44-VGPR kernel supports more wave overlap.
annotations.suggestion: These are upstream optimization opportunities; token-wave's atomic pair is already cheaper and is not its primary bottleneck.

annotations.title: Sorted GEMM2 has a 63.7% LDS conflict ratio
annotations.note: PMC records 310,272 bank conflicts and 796,992 LDS index-active events, a 63.7% conflict ratio under WaveScope's metric. Token-wave GEMM2 is only 1.61%. The baseline wins despite this, reinforcing that work reduction and latency hiding dominate the comparison.
